title: GCP-OASE & Scion: Team-Based, Provenance-Locked Pre-Clinical R&D on Google Cloud

scenes.title: Why Single-Player Chatbot Science Fails Governance
scenes.tts_script: Welcome to the Google Cloud Scion and O-A-S-E Workshop, the Open Agentic Science Engine. In early drug discovery, traditional rigid pipelines and single-player chatbots both fall short. Fixed pipelines break whenever new lab data takes an unexpected turn. At the same time, unguarded chatbots can make up numbers, gloss over safety warnings, and repeat the blind spots of a single model.

scenes.title: Scion + OASE Value Proposition & Multi-Model Projects
scenes.tts_script: Google Cloud Scion and the Science Engine solve this by turning discovery into a governed team sport. Scion's central Hub coordinates shared projects across web interfaces, developer workspaces, and the command line. Because Scion is model-agnostic, agents powered by Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI can review and challenge each other's work. And when a team needs to wait for real laboratory results, Scion cleanly pauses the session and picks right back up weeks later.

scenes.title: 4-Tier Agent Roster, 9-State Work Orders & Two-Phase Latch
scenes.tts_script: Inside each project, twenty-two specialized agent roles divide the work between coordinators, domain scientists, and independent reviewers. No specialist is allowed to grade its own homework in plain text. Every scientific step runs in two locked phases. Phase one saves the raw data files with tamper-proof digital fingerprints. Phase two checks those results offline against clear, pre-defined quality standards.

scenes.title: Stages 0-1: Ranking Ideas & Checking Human Genetics (WO-001..003)
scenes.tts_script: Let's watch this team tackle a real-world challenge on Google Cloud: designing an oral pill to lower cholesterol. In the first two stages, the agents rank competing biological ideas and check human genetic databases to confirm the target is both effective and safe to block. Even when the target passes, the system automatically flags potential liver and kidney questions so the next team must investigate them.

scenes.title: Stages 2-4: Mapping a Binding Pocket & Catching a Heart Safety Trap (WO-004..007)
scenes.tts_script: Next, the structural biology and chemistry agents map a binding pocket on the target protein and test candidate molecules. The top-scoring molecule binds strongly, and an ordinary chatbot would stop right there and declare success. Instead, the Science Engine's safety checks catch three red flags, including a serious heart-rhythm risk. The team automatically pivots to a safer backup family and selects a clean candidate for a once-daily pill.

scenes.title: Mechanical Governance Teeth: 4 Adversarial Tamper Drills
scenes.tts_script: To prove these guardrails are real, we run four deliberate tamper tests. Every work order must pass ten automated checks before its findings can move forward. Across four stress tests, we alter a data file, inflate a score, delete a safety warning, and remove a grading rule. In every single case, the verification gate catches the change and blocks promotion immediately.

scenes.title: The Complete Picture & 31-Page Stage-Gate Dossier (WO-008)
scenes.tts_script: In the final stage, the curator agent brings together all eight verified work orders and eleven safety handoffs. It builds a complete decision package along with a thirty-one page interactive evidence portal. Every single number in the final summary links directly back to the exact data file that produced it on Google Cloud.

scenes.title: Architecture Scorecard & Field Takeaways
scenes.tts_script: Running this end-to-end campaign on Google Cloud highlights a simple takeaway. Software guardrails never replace real laboratory experiments. But combining Google Cloud Scion's multi-model teamwork with the Science Engine's automated verification stops silent errors before they spread. Together, they make AI-assisted research transparent, repeatable, and ready for real scientific review.
